text: Just at that moment. <break time="0.8s" /> A beautifully dressed boy and girl. <break time="0.8s" /> Sat down where the old couple had been and they were the hero and heroine, of course. <break time="0.8s" /> Still smiling. <break time="0.8s" /> Miss Brill prepared to listen. <break time="0.8s" /> But the girl said, No, not now. <break time="0.8s" /> And the boy asked, But why. <break time="0.8s" /> Because of that stupid old thing at the end there. <break time="0.8s" /> Why does she come here at all. <break time="0.8s" /> And who wants her, he went on Why does she not keep her silly old face at home. <break time="0.8s" /> It is her fu fur which is so funny. <break time="0.8s" /> The girl giggled. <break time="0.8s" /> It is exactly like a fried whiting. <break time="0.8s" /> On her way home. <break time="0.8s" /> Miss Brill usually bought a slice of honey cake. <break time="0.8s" /> At the bakers. <break time="0.8s" /> And it was her Sunday treat. <break time="0.8s" /> Sometimes with an almond in it. <break time="0.8s" /> And sometimes not. <break time="0.8s" /> When there was an almond. <break time="0.8s" /> It was like carrying home a tiny present. <break time="0.8s" /> And she would hurry home. <break time="0.8s" /> And strike the match for the kettle. <break time="0.8s" /> In quite a dashing way. <break time="0.8s" /> But today she passed the bakers by climbed the stairs. <break time="0.8s" /> Went into her little dark room. <break time="0.8s" /> Which was like a cupboard. <break time="0.8s" /> And sat down on the red eiderdown. <break time="0.8s" /> She sat there a long time. <break time="0.8s" /> Then quickly, without looking. <break time="0.8s" /> Laid the fur inside its box. <break time="0.8s" /> And when she put the lid on she thought she heard something crying.
